messages.subject: readr not reading milliseconds correctly?
messages.body_plain:
I have a question about reading a file with read_csv. I have times that look like this with hours, minutes, seconds and milliseconds:

6:19:43.722

When I use read_csv in readr to read them using col_time("%H:%M:%OS") it reads hours, minutes, and seconds just fine, but there are no milliseconds. I pulled  getOption("digits.secs") to see how many digits on seconds should be displayed, but it says 3, as I’d like.

When I print out what I’ve read, it looks like
         DATE  TIME_M PRICE
1  2014-01-02 6:19:43 75.10
2  2014-01-02 6:19:49 75.10
3  2014-01-02 7:00:07 75.07

When I assign that first time to a variable and print it, I get 22783 which is the number of seconds since midnight—so no milliseconds.

To confuse things, if I try:
d<-"6:19:43.722"
> strptime(d,"%H:%M:%OS")
[1] "2016-03-07 06:19:43.722 EST"

strptime will strip that character vector just fine… just read_csv won’t with col_time. I have a very large dataset and I'd like to read it in with time correctly so I don't have to run through it again. Any thoughts?

Thanks

messages.subject: mutate_ and lubridate::parse_date_time SE not working together as expected
messages.subject_clean: mutate_ and lubridate::parse_date_time SE not working together as expected
messages.body_plain:
Consider:
``` R
df <- frame_data( ~ start_date,
                    "07/15/2015 15:39",
                    "07/15/2015 15:42")

df_NSE <- df %>%
          mutate(response_date = parse_date_time(start_date, orders ="mdY hm"))
```

I would have thought that something like the following would be a standard-evaluation equivalent:
``` R
var_name <- "start_date"
df_SE_expected_to_work <- df %>%
          mutate_(response_date = ~parse_date_time(var_name, orders ="mdY hm"))
```
but this just throws a warning and just has blank rows for the response_date column:
```R
Warning message:
All formats failed to parse. No formats found.
```
I tried many variations even with interp, just to make sure it wasnt my understanding of NSE such as this one:
``` R
df_SE_interp_expected_to_work <- df %>%
          mutate_(response_date = interp(~parse_date_time(var_name, orders ="mdY hm"), var_name = var_name))
```
but i get the same outcome

I was able to hack a working solution for both cases:
``` R
df_SE_working <- df %>%
          mutate_(response_date = ~parse_date_time(df[[var_name]], orders ="mdY hm"))
df_SE_interp_working <- df %>%
          mutate_(response_date = interp(~parse_date_time(df[[var_name]], orders ="mdY hm"), var_name = var_name))
```

messages.subject_clean: Problems with SE, mutate_each_, and variables with spaces
messages.body_plain:
This has rather been driving me crazy. It should be straightforward but it's giving me lots of problems.
I have a data frame with variables that I want to summarize by two classification variables. The variables to summarize are

demo_vars <- c("Pct ELL", "Pct Free/Reduced Lunch", "Pct White", "Pct Afr-Am", "Pct Latino", "Pct Asian")

The code I'm trying to run is:

    the.var.m <- demo_by_schl %>%
    group_by(level, schl_id) %>%
        summarize_each_(funs(mean), demo_vars)

But when I try this I get this error message:

Error in parse(text = x) : <text>:1:5: unexpected symbol
1: Pct ELL
        ^

Is this because of the space in the variable name? If so, how do I get around it? If not, what else am I doing wrong?

TIA.
--
Stuart Luppescu -- pixbuf .at. gmail.com <http://gmail.com>
I made up a new word: plagiarism.
  --jpuller

B

messages.subject: Re: aaply example from JSS article fails with error - typo or bug?
messages.subject_clean: aaply example from JSS article fails with error - typo or bug?
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I'm resurrecting this thread even though it's been dead for a while...

I came across the same problem, as I have been learning about plyr as we have been using dplyr in a course that I am taking (basically helps me to understand the big picture).

I tried to work through the examples in the JStatSoft paper and came across the following issue:

> library(plyr)
> data(ozone)

> month <- ordered(rep(1:12, length = 72))

> library(MASS)

> deseasf <- function(value) rlm(value ~ month - 1)
> models <- aaply(ozone, 1:2, deseasf)

Error: Results must have one or more dimensions.

In addition: There were 14 warnings (use warnings() to see them)
> sessionInfo()
R version 3.2.3 (2015-12-10)
Platform: x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu (64-bit)

locale:
 [1] LC_CTYPE=en_US.UTF-8       LC_NUMERIC=C
 [3] LC_TIME=en_US.UTF-8        LC_COLLATE=en_US.UTF-8
 [5] LC_MONETARY=en_US.UTF-8    LC_MESSAGES=en_US.UTF-8
 [7] LC_PAPER=en_US.UTF-8       LC_NAME=C
 [9] LC_ADDRESS=C               LC_TELEPHONE=C
[11] LC_MEASUREMENT=en_US.UTF-8 LC_IDENTIFICATION=C

attached base packages:
[1] stats     graphics  grDevices utils     datasets  methods   base

other attached packages:
[1] MASS_7.3-45 plyr_1.8.2

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
[1] tools_3.2.3 Rcpp_0.12.3

I went back to the version of R that was current at the time of the JStatSoft paper:

> library(plyr)
> library(MASS)
> data(ozone)

> month <- ordered(rep(1:12, length = 72))

> deseasf <- function(value) rlm(value ~ month - 1)
> models <- aaply(ozone, 1:2, deseasf)

There were 14 warnings (use warnings() to see them)
> dim(models)
[1] 24 24
> is.list(models)
[1] TRUE
> is.array(models)
[1] TRUE
> sessionInfo()
R version 2.12.0 (2010-10-15)
Platform: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (64-bit)

locale:
 [1] LC_CTYPE=en_US.UTF-8       LC_NUMERIC=C
 [3] LC_TIME=en_US.UTF-8        LC_COLLATE=en_US.UTF-8
 [5] LC_MONETARY=C              LC_MESSAGES=C
 [7] LC_PAPER=en_US.UTF-8       LC_NAME=C
 [9] LC_ADDRESS=C               LC_TELEPHONE=C
[11] LC_MEASUREMENT=en_US.UTF-8 LC_IDENTIFICATION=C

attached base packages:
[1] stats     graphics  grDevices utils     datasets  methods   base

other attached packages:
[1] MASS_7.3-8 plyr_1.4.1

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
[1] tools_2.12.0

Basically, to cut a long story short (I checked all the versions of plyr with the requisite versions of R up to plyr-1.8.0), the bug was introduced in plyr v1.8.0.

I forked and cloned the plyr git repository and have had a go at fixing the code... all the unit tests pass including two new tests where I try to produce the bug when trying to generate an array list.

I have submitted a "pull request" <https://github.com/hadley/plyr/pull/273> to github, hopefully all the code is acceptable and if anyone's first introduction to plyr is via the JStatSoft paper, the first line of plyr-related code won't produce an error!

Take care,
Rob Pollock.

> > > extracting the residuals.
> >
> > I actually don't think alply is what we should be using. Hadley
> > motivates the example by saying: "It would also be nice to keep the
> > models in a 2d list-array, so we can reference a local model (model[[1,
> > 1]]) in a similar way to referencing a local time series (ozone[1, 1,
> > ]); keeping data-structures consistent reduces cognitive effort."
> >
> > Using alply() as a workaround to create an intermediate list of models
> > doesn't do this. In fact if I use alply() there is no straightforward
> > way to get the model associated with a particular location. On the other
> > hand using the built-in apply() function works almost like Hadley
> > describes (e.g. in the example I provided models2[1,1][[1]])
> >
> > > Alternatively, you could rewrite the
> > > function to extract the residuals from the fitted model object and
> > > return them directly since resid() is an extraction function. This
> > > works for me with the current version of plyr:
> > >
> > > deseasf <- function(value) resid(rlm(value ~ month - 1))
> > > deseas <- aaply(ozone, 1:2, deseasf)
> >
> > But the point of the example is that one would want to create the
> > intermediate object of models in an array that matches the input. And
> > the same could be done with apply by replacing aaply() with apply() in
> > your example.
> >
> > > On Sun, Dec 21, 2014 at 7:32 AM, Manuel Morales <mmor...@williams.edu> wrote:
> > > > I'm looking into using the plyr family of functions and started out by
> > > > reading Hadley's article "The Split-Apply-Combine Strategy of Data
> > > > Manipulation"
> > > >
> > > > The first example in the article is:
> > > >
> > > > library(MASS)
> > > > library(plyr)
> > > >
> > > > deseasf <- function(value) rlm(value ~ month - 1)
> > > >
> > > > models <- aaply(ozone, 1:2, deseasf)
> > > > deseaf <- aaply(ozone, 1:2, deseasf)
> > > >
> > > > But the first call to aaply fails with the error message: "Error:
> > > > Results must have one or more dimensions."
> > > >
> > > > Note that I can use the built-in apply functions to do this and it works
> > > > fine, although the output array needs to be reorganized:
> > > >
> > > > models2 <- apply(ozone, 1:2, deseasf)
> > > > deseas2 <- apply(models2, 1:2, function(x) resid(x[[1]]))
> > > > deseas2 <- aperm(deseas2,(c(2,3,1)))
> > > >
> > > > On StackOverflow it was suggested that the example in the article was a
> > > > typo and it should have been:
> > > >
> > > > models <- alply(ozone, 1:2, deseasf)
> > > > deseaf <- laply(ozone, deseasf)
> > > >
> > > > But then the whole point of saving the intermediate object models is
> > > > lost since it doesn't preserve the dimensionality of the original object
> > > > (like I think was intended and as the apply example above does).
> > > >
> > > > My guess is that this behavior isn't intended but maybe I'm making a
> > > > simple mistake?
> > > >
> > > > Thanks!
> > > > Manuel
> > > >
